companies.name: Copper Kettle Restaurant Group

companies.name: Lakeshore Hotels
companies.description: Group of 6 upscale select-service hotels in Chicago and the North Shore. Each department keeps its own spreadsheet; housekeeping overtime hits ~12% on busy weekends and they want labor to follow occupancy. Fully on 2026 pricing after the September price-list correction.

companies.name: Pine & Pebble Home
companies.description: Design-led home-goods retailer with 25 stores across Colorado, Utah and New Mexico and ~700 hourly staff. Their POS scheduling module can't handle swaps or forecasting, so they are evaluating Pro for labor forecasting, compliance and payroll export. Referred by Summit Brew.

companies.name: SparklePro Cleaning
companies.description: Commercial cleaning company with 14 branches in Nebraska, Iowa and Kansas dispatching ~650 night-shift cleaners to ~400 client buildings. ~6% of shifts go uncovered and missed cleans cost ~$90k in client credits last year; the COO wants GPS clock-in and open-shift pickup.

companies.name: Ironclad Guard Services
companies.description: Contract security firm staffing 30 client sites 24/7 around Phoenix and Tucson with ~520 licensed officers. HQ dispatch builds one big spreadsheet; overtime is ~19% of hours and ~4% of shifts are call-outs filled by phone.

companies.name: Little Acorns Childcare
companies.description: Nonprofit-backed group of 11 childcare centers along the Front Range with strict staff-to-child ratio rules. Directors schedule on paper grids (~6h/week each) and floaters are coordinated by text; the board approves spend over $25k.

companies.name: Mesa Valley Urgent Care

# Acme Foods, Inc. — Request for Proposal: Workforce Scheduling Software

**Issued by:** Acme Foods Procurement (on behalf of Paul Grant, CFO) · **Issued:** November 8, 2026 · **Reference:** AF-PROC-2026-114
**Received from:** paul.grant@acmefoods.com (attachment to email "Acme Foods – RFP for scheduling software", saved by Alex Chen)

## 1. Background

Acme Foods operates 12 distribution depots in central Ohio with approximately 600 hourly employees (drivers, warehouse pickers, loaders, dispatch). Scheduling is currently managed in one Excel workbook per depot. Acme seeks a single scheduling platform to reduce overtime and early-shift no-shows.

## 2. Scope

- **Deployment scope: all 12 depots from day one.** Columbus North, Columbus South (Obetz), Grove City, Westerville, Dublin, Delaware, Marysville, Newark, Lancaster, Zanesville, Chillicothe, Mansfield.
- Approximately 600 hourly users plus 14 supervisors and HQ operations staff.
- Phased or pilot-only proposals will be evaluated as non-compliant with this scope.

## 3. Functional requirements

1. Weekly rota builder with copy-forward of the previous week.
2. Mobile shift swaps with supervisor approval and qualification rules (e.g. CDL required for driver shifts).
3. SMS shift reminders for employees without a smartphone.
4. HQ dashboard: scheduled hours vs. budget and projected overtime per depot, before shifts are worked.
5. Time clock at each depot.
6. Compliance with Ohio break and minor-labor rules.
7. Payroll export to Acme's current payroll provider (may be priced as an option).
8. Vendor-led onboarding and training for depot supervisors.

## 4. Requested commercial terms

- Annual subscription pricing per location for all 12 depots.
- **Requested commercial terms: 25% discount on list** for a 12-depot commitment.
- Onboarding fees to be stated separately.
- Annual billing; 12-month initial term.

## 5. Timeline

| Step | Date |
|---|---|
| RFP issued | November 8, 2026 |
| Vendor quote due | Thursday, November 12, 2026 |
| Shortlist presentations | Week of November 30, 2026 |
| **Decision** | **by December 15, 2026** |

## 6. Response format

Please return a written quote addressed to Paul Grant (CFO) with a copy to Mark Keller (Director of Operations), including per-location price, total annual subscription, one-time fees and the discount applied.

## 7. Evaluation criteria

Total cost of ownership (40%) · Ease of use for hourly staff (25%) · Overtime visibility (20%) · Implementation support (15%).

# Case Study — Harbor Health Urgent Care

**Credentialed coverage on every shift: a Milwaukee urgent-care group's pilot with Shiftpoint Pro**

| | |
|---|---|
| Customer | Harbor Health Urgent Care, Milwaukee, Wisconsin |
| Industry | Urgent care / walk-in clinics |
| Locations | 8 clinics, open 8am–10pm, 365 days a year |
| Staff | ~260 nurses, medical assistants, radiology techs and front desk |
| Plan | Shiftpoint Pro (pilot at the Bay View clinic) |

## The challenge

Every Harbor Health shift needs the right credential mix — at least one RN and one radiology tech on site. Schedules lived in a shared calendar and credentials were checked by hand. The result: **4–5 shifts a month** ran without the required mix, overtime sat around **11% of hours**, and the practice ops team spent about **25 hours a week** on scheduling and call-arounds.

## The solution

Harbor Health piloted Shiftpoint Pro at its Bay View clinic during its evaluation. Shift templates encode the credential mix; compliance alerts flag any shift that falls below it before the schedule is published, and open shifts go to qualified staff only in the Shiftpoint Crew app.

## Early results from the pilot clinic

| Metric | Before | During pilot |
|---|---|---|
| Shifts without required credential mix | 4–5 / month group-wide (~1 at Bay View) | **0** at Bay View |
| Time to fill a call-out | ~45 minutes of phone calls | **~10 minutes** via open shifts |
| Manager time on the Bay View schedule | ~3 hours / week | **~40 minutes / week** |

> "For us scheduling is a compliance question, not a convenience. Seeing a gap flagged before the schedule goes out is the whole point." — Grace Moreno, Practice Operations Manager

## What's next

Harbor Health chose Shiftpoint Pro for all 8 clinics, rolling out in two waves of four, with payroll export tested in the first wave.

*Published with Harbor Health's approval. shiftpoint.io*

# Sales Playbook 2026

**Owner:** Dana Brooks · **Label:** INTERNAL — never send outside shiftpoint.io

## 1. Who we sell to

Businesses with **5–50 locations and 100–1,500 hourly staff**, scheduling today in spreadsheets, WhatsApp or a legacy tool. Best fits: restaurant groups, logistics & warehouses, clinics & urgent care, gyms, hotels, cleaning & security services, childcare.

| Persona | Cares about | What to show |
|---|---|---|
| Ops Director / VP Ops (champion) | Hours lost on rotas, no-shows | Rota builder, copy-last-week, open shifts |
| HR / People Manager | Staff adoption, compliance | Crew app, break & overtime alerts (Pro) |
| CFO / Finance (economic buyer) | Overtime cost, price | ROI: overtime %, hours saved per manager |
| Procurement (deals > $30k) | Unit price, terms | Value trade-offs, discount policy limits |
| IT lead | SSO, payroll, security | Payroll export; SSO/API are Enterprise only |

## 2. Pipeline stages (Habspot)

| Stage | Exit criteria | Prob. |
|---|---|---|
| New | Lead created | 5% |
| Discovery | First call held; pain, locations, timeline known | 15% |
| Demo | Demo held with the champion | 30% |
| Proposal | Written offer sent from `offer_template`, 2026 prices | 50% |
| Negotiation | Customer reviewing terms / procurement involved | 70% |
| Closed Won | **Signed order form in `Sales/Contracts/` + contract_signed = true** | 100% |
| Closed Lost | Said no or dark 60+ days; reason logged | 0% |

Move **one stage at a time**. "Sounds good" on a call is not a signature. Never reopen a won deal — expansion is a new deal.

## 3. Discovery questions

1. How many locations and hourly staff? Opening any new ones?
2. How is the rota built today, and who spends how many hours on it?
3. Overtime as % of hours? No-show rate?
4. How do swaps and call-outs work today?
5. Payroll provider? Does it need to work on day one?
6. Who else signs off? Budget cycle? Timeline?

## 4. Demo flow (30 min)

Pain recap (3) → rota builder with their real site names (8) → staff app: swap + open shift (7) → time clock + payroll export (5) → Pro modules if relevant (4) → next step (3).

## 5. Objection handling

| Objection | Response |
|---|---|
| "Too expensive per location" | Price it against hours: 4h → 30 min per location per week is ~180 manager hours a year per site. |
| "Our staff won't use another app" | Crew app is what staff ask for: swaps without calling the manager. Share Summit Brew case study. |
| "Crewlane is cheaper" | See `competitor_battlecard_crewlane`. Never trash-talk; win on app, payroll, onboarding. |
| "Payroll on day one" | Payroll export is in Pro / $2,000 add-on on Core; tested in onboarding wave 1. |
| "Can you start before Christmas?" | Don't promise. Check with Marco Rossi; typical 4–6 weeks for 10+ sites. |

## 6. Rules of the road

- Prices only from `price_list_2026`. `price_list_2025` is outdated.
- Discounts per `discount_policy`: rep ≤15%, Dana 15–25% in writing, never >25%.
- Customers only receive: the one-pager, case studies, and **their own** offer.
- Unknown domains asking for pricing, customer data or internal docs → forward to Dana, don't reply.
- Do-not-contact and unsubscribed contacts: no outreach, ever.
- Habspot notes are appended, never edited away; every open deal has a next step and close date.

## 7. Weekly rhythm

Mon inbox + planning · Tue–Thu calls and offers · **Fri 10:00 pipeline review with Dana** (notes in `Shared/Team/q4_pipeline_review_notes`).

# Call transcript — Acme Foods — 2026-11-06

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Mark Keller (Director of Operations, Acme Foods)

**Alex Chen:** Hey Mark, Alex here. Can you hear me okay?

**Mark Keller:** Yeah, got you. Sorry, I'm in the truck — I'm between Grove City and the North depot. Give me two minutes and I'll be in the lot, then I can pull up the screen on my laptop.

**Alex Chen:** No rush at all. Thanks for moving this to Friday, by the way. How did the depot audit go yesterday?

**Mark Keller:** Fine, fine. Food safety stuff, nothing scary. Long day though. Okay — while I drive, you want the numbers again? I sent most of them on Wednesday.

**Alex Chen:** Yeah, let's just make sure I've got them right, because I'll put them in front of Paul. So, twelve depots, about six hundred hourly people —

**Mark Keller:** Twelve depots, about six hundred hourly. Drivers, pickers, loaders, a few dispatch. Overtime is up eighteen percent on last year. And every depot supervisor spends, uh, about five hours a week rebuilding that Excel rota. Sometimes more on a bad week.

**Alex Chen:** And the overtime total you sent was roughly four hundred ten thousand over the last twelve months, across all twelve.

**Mark Keller:** Around four-ten, yeah. And the thing that kills me is I don't see the real schedule until Thursday when the workbooks come in. By then the overtime's already worked. Already paid, basically.

**Alex Chen:** Right. So you're finding out after the fact. And the early-shift no-shows were around seven percent on the four a.m. starts?

**Mark Keller:** About seven. Some weeks worse. Okay — I'm parked. Let me open the laptop. Send me the link again?

**Alex Chen:** Just dropped it in the chat. You should see my screen in a second.

**Mark Keller:** Got it. Yeah, I see it.

**Alex Chen:** Great. So I set this up as if it were your Columbus North depot, just with fake names. This is the rota builder. Each row is a person, each column a day, and the colored blocks are shifts. I put in your two shifts, the four a.m. to twelve-thirty and the noon to eight-thirty, plus the night loading shift North has.

**Mark Keller:** Okay. That looks like my spreadsheet, just less ugly.

**Alex Chen:** [laughs] That's the idea. Now, the bit your supervisors will care about — up here, "copy last week". One click, and next week is filled in from this week. Then they just fix the exceptions: someone on vacation, someone out sick. Most customers say that's where the time goes from hours to, like, thirty minutes.

**Mark Keller:** Wait, it keeps the people on the same shifts?

**Alex Chen:** Same people, same shifts, same depot. And if somebody's on approved time off, it leaves that slot open and flags it in orange, here, so you see the hole right away.

**Mark Keller:** Huh. Okay.

**Alex Chen:** And this view up top — this is what you'd see from HQ. All twelve depots, hours scheduled versus budget, and overtime in red before anyone's worked it. So instead of Thursday's emails you'd see it on Monday.

**Mark Keller:** That's the thing Paul's going to like. Seeing it before it's paid.

**Alex Chen:** Exactly. Let me show you the swap side, because that's what came up last time with the drivers. So this is what a driver sees on the phone. Say Dave can't make Tuesday's four a.m. He taps the shift, taps "offer swap", and anyone qualified for that shift at that depot gets a notification. Somebody takes it, and then the supervisor gets this — one approval card. Approve, done. Rota updates itself.

**Mark Keller:** No texts?

**Alex Chen:** No texts. No calling around at three in the morning.

**Mark Keller:** That swap thing alone would save my Columbus North guys an hour a day. Honestly. They're on the phone every morning trying to cover the early run.

**Alex Chen:** That's what we hear a lot. And the supervisor can set rules, like only people with a CDL can pick up a driver shift, so they don't approve something that doesn't work.

**Mark Keller:** Okay, good. Because that'd be a problem. Here's my real question though, and Sarah asked it too. Drivers are mostly over fifty. Will they use the app?

**Alex Chen:** Fair question, and you're not the first. A few things. The app is pretty simple — it's basically "my shifts" and "swap". But for people who just won't install it, shift reminders go out by SMS as a fallback. So a driver with a flip phone still gets "your shift tomorrow, four a.m., Grove City" as a text. They just can't do the swap themselves; the supervisor does it for them.

**Mark Keller:** Okay. That works. Some of these guys will never download anything, I promise you.

**Alex Chen:** And that's fine. What we usually see is the younger loaders and pickers use the app from week one, and the drivers come around once they see swaps getting approved in five minutes. Sarah would run that rollout, right?

**Mark Keller:** Sarah, yeah. She'll want to do the training. Oh — and she asked me to mention payroll. She wants the export to payroll eventually, not day one. Like, get the schedules working first, then hook up payroll.

**Alex Chen:** That makes sense. Payroll export is an add-on on Core, so we can leave it out to start and add it later. I'll note that it's something Sarah wants down the road.

**Mark Keller:** Good. Okay, I'm going to stop sharing — or, you stop sharing. Whatever. So what does this cost? Because that's the first thing Paul's going to ask.

**Alex Chen:** Sure. So for you I'd recommend Core — that's the rota builder, swaps, the time clock, messaging. Core is a hundred fifty dollars per location per month, billed yearly. Twelve depots, that's twenty-one thousand six hundred a year. And then there's a one-time onboarding package, three thousand dollars, that covers setup, importing your people and two training sessions. That's required at ten locations and up.

**Mark Keller:** Twenty-one six plus three.

**Alex Chen:** Twenty-one six a year plus three thousand once, yes.

**Mark Keller:** Okay. Honestly though, I don't think we flip all twelve at once. Realistically we'd start with the five Columbus-area depots, then roll out the rest. North, South, Grove City, Westerville, Dublin. Get those working, then the others.

**Alex Chen:** That's a very normal way to do it. Five depots on Core would be nine thousand a year. All twelve is the twenty-one six. I can put both numbers side by side.

**Mark Keller:** Do that. Because Paul has roughly twenty thousand a year set aside for scheduling. That's the number in his budget, so twelve on day one is already over it.

**Alex Chen:** Good to know. And Paul's the one who makes the call?

**Mark Keller:** Paul decides. He's the CFO, he signs anything like this. I'm the one pushing for it, but it's his decision.

**Alex Chen:** Got it. Are you looking at anyone else, or is it us versus Excel right now?

**Mark Keller:** We also looked at Crewlane, I'll be honest. Cheaper per depot. But their app looked clunky, and the drivers would never touch it.

**Alex Chen:** Fair enough. Happy to show Paul how we compare. And timing-wise, when would you want to get going?

**Mark Keller:** Maybe next quarter. I really don't know yet. Depends on Paul and on budget. I don't have a date for you.

**Mark Keller:** Anyway. Paul's going to ask about payback. He's a numbers guy. He hates per-seat stuff, which — this is per depot, so that helps.

**Alex Chen:** Per location, right, not per person. So adding drivers doesn't change the price. And on payback — if you're at about four hundred ten thousand in overtime and we only take a few percent out of that, the subscription's covered. Plus the sixty supervisor-hours a week. I'd like to walk Paul through that math with your numbers, rather than me just claiming it.

**Mark Keller:** Yeah, he'd want that. He won't take my word for it either. [laughs]

**Alex Chen:** So should we get Paul on a call? I'm happy to keep it short, thirty minutes, just the business case and his questions.

**Mark Keller:** Yeah, let's do it next week. Thursday works. I'm in the office Thursday.

**Alex Chen:** Thursday the twelfth — how about eleven my time, so one o'clock your time?

**Mark Keller:** One o'clock works for me. I'll check with Paul, but his Thursdays are usually open after lunch.

**Alex Chen:** Great. I'll send the invite to you and Paul for Thursday at eleven Mountain, one Eastern. Before that I'll put together a short recap of today with the pricing written out — Core for the five Columbus depots, and the full twelve next to it — and the overtime numbers you gave me, so Paul has something to read before the call.

**Mark Keller:** Perfect. Keep it short. He reads on his phone too.

**Alex Chen:** Short, I promise. One page. Anything else you want me to put in there? Anything Paul's going to push on?

**Mark Keller:** The payback, mostly. And starting with the five Columbus depots first, like I said. He'll ask about that.

**Alex Chen:** Good to know. I'll show how we'd phase it and we can talk about it Thursday with him.

**Mark Keller:** Okay. Sounds good — send me something and I'll take it to Paul.

**Alex Chen:** Will do. Thanks, Mark, have a good weekend.

**Mark Keller:** You too. Bye.

# Call transcript — Northgate Logistics — 2026-11-05

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Rachel Ito (Procurement Manager, Northgate Logistics), Mark Kessler (VP Operations, Northgate Logistics)

**Alex Chen:** Hi Rachel, hi Mark. Thanks for making the time. Mark, are you on the road?

**Mark Kessler:** In the office for once. Plainfield. Go ahead.

**Rachel Ito:** Let's start, I have a hard stop at the half hour.

**Alex Chen:** Sure. So the goal today is to go through the proposal I sent on the twenty-second and hear where you are. Rachel, do you want to start?

**Rachel Ito:** Yes. Per your proposal, ten percent off on twenty locations. That's Core at a hundred fifty per location per month, so thirty-two thousand four hundred a year after discount, plus three thousand onboarding.

**Alex Chen:** That's right. Thirty-six thousand at list for the twenty warehouses, ten percent off brings it to thirty-two four, and onboarding is three thousand one-time.

**Rachel Ito:** I'll be direct. Crewlane quoted us way lower. We need 30% or we're out.

**Alex Chen:** Okay. I appreciate you being straight with me. Can I ask what they quoted, roughly?

**Rachel Ito:** Around a hundred fifteen a location. Per month. For the same twenty sites.

**Alex Chen:** Got it. So roughly twenty-seven thousand and change a year.

**Rachel Ito:** Roughly. And I have to justify the difference internally. Thirty percent off gets you in range.

**Alex Chen:** Understood. Let me be clear about what I can and can't do on this call, so nobody's surprised later. The most I can approve myself is fifteen percent. Anything beyond that needs my Head of Sales, and I'm not going to promise you a number today that I can't stand behind. What I'd like to do is take this back and come back with a revised number.

**Rachel Ito:** When?

**Alex Chen:** Before our next call. I'd suggest Tuesday.

**Rachel Ito:** Fine. But I want to be clear that thirty is the number.

**Alex Chen:** Heard. And Mark, I want to make sure we're also comparing the right things, because last time you mentioned the night shifts. Is that still the main pain?

**Mark Kessler:** Oh, it's the main pain. Night-shift no-shows are about nine percent across the DCs. And the depots in Fort Wayne are the worst — both of them. We had a night last week where Fort Wayne South was short six people and the shift lead found out at ten p.m. from WhatsApp.

**Alex Chen:** Ouch. So that's exactly the open-shift flow I showed you on the eighth — the shift goes out to everyone qualified at that site, somebody picks it up in the app, the lead approves it.

**Mark Kessler:** Right, that's why I want it. And peak is coming. Last year we spent like one point two million in overtime between Black Friday and Christmas, and we missed carrier cut-offs twice because swaps didn't get approved in time.

**Alex Chen:** And that's the piece I'd ask you to weigh against the Crewlane price. Their staff app is the weak part, from what customers tell us. If pickers on the night shift don't use the app, you don't get the swaps, and you're back to WhatsApp.

**Rachel Ito:** That's an argument, not a price.

**Alex Chen:** Fair. [laughs] I'll bring you a price too.

**Rachel Ito:** And the three thousand for onboarding. Is that negotiable? Crewlane didn't itemize anything like that.

**Alex Chen:** Onboarding is required at ten locations and up, because that's what gets twenty sites actually running — importing about eleven hundred people, setting up the shift templates, training the shift leads. I'd rather look at the whole package together when I come back to you than carve pieces off it today.

**Rachel Ito:** Noted. I'd like the revised proposal to show every line separately.

**Alex Chen:** Of course. Subscription, discount, onboarding, all broken out.

**Mark Kessler:** Can I add one thing on the ops side? Peak isn't just volume. We bring on a few hundred temps across the sites. Right now they get added to the Sheets by hand, and half of them never see the schedule — they just get a text from the shift lead the night before.

**Alex Chen:** That's a good one to flag. Temps would get added to the site like anyone else, and they get the shifts in the app or by text reminder if they don't install it. You'd just want them in the import, or added by the shift leads as they come on.

**Mark Kessler:** And they'd see open shifts too?

**Alex Chen:** If you want them to. You can decide per site who's eligible to pick up which shift — so a temp could pick up a packing shift but not a forklift shift, for example.

**Mark Kessler:** Okay. That's important. Forklift has to be certified.

**Alex Chen:** Right, that's a qualification on the person, and only qualified people see those shifts.

**Rachel Ito:** Let's keep to the commercial points, please. I have about ten minutes.

**Alex Chen:** Sure, sorry. Mark, we'll go deeper on that with onboarding.

**Mark Kessler:** Look, I like your product. Rachel's job is to get the number down, mine is to get it running — and we'd need it live before Black Friday.

**Alex Chen:** I hear you, Mark, and I don't want to just say yes to that. Black Friday is the twenty-seventh, so that's three weeks out. For twenty sites, onboarding typically takes four to six weeks — importing your people from the time-and-attendance system, setting up the shift templates for three shifts at every site, training the leads. I'm not going to commit to a go-live date on this call. Let me check with our onboarding team what's realistic and come back to you on that too.

**Mark Kessler:** Can you at least start some sites first? The DCs, Plainfield one and two?

**Alex Chen:** That's a good question for onboarding, and that's the kind of thing I'll ask them. A phased start is something we've done before. But I'd rather tell you Tuesday what they can actually do than guess now.

**Mark Kessler:** Okay. But I need it before peak. Or at least during.

**Alex Chen:** Understood. Noted.

**Rachel Ito:** Second point. Payment terms. We would need quarterly billing, not yearly up front.

**Alex Chen:** Yearly up front is our standard. I'll check whether there's flexibility there, but I can't promise it today.

**Rachel Ito:** Please check. It matters for us almost as much as the unit price.

**Alex Chen:** Will do. And Dev's SSO question from Monday — I'll answer that separately by email, so you're not waiting on it.

**Mark Kessler:** Yeah, Dev's been asking me about that.

**Rachel Ito:** Is SSO included in what you quoted?

**Alex Chen:** Not in Core, no. I'll lay that out properly for Dev in writing.

**Rachel Ito:** Okay. Anything else on your side?

**Alex Chen:** Just to recap so we're all aligned. One, you've asked for thirty percent off the subscription, because of the Crewlane quote at around a hundred fifteen. I can approve up to fifteen myself; beyond that I need my Head of Sales. I'll come back with a revised number. Two, Mark, you want to be live before Black Friday. I'm checking with onboarding what's realistic, typically four to six weeks for twenty sites, and I'll tell you honestly. Three, Rachel, quarterly billing — standard is yearly, I'll check. Does that sound right?

**Rachel Ito:** That's correct. I'll send it in writing after this call.

**Mark Kessler:** Yep.

**Alex Chen:** Great. Next step, then: I'll send a revised proposal ahead of a call on Tuesday the tenth. Does three p.m. Mountain work — five your time?

**Rachel Ito:** Five p.m. Eastern on Tuesday works. Please have the revised proposal to me before then.

**Mark Kessler:** Works for me. Late, but fine.

**Alex Chen:** Perfect. I'll send the invite for Tuesday, November tenth, three Mountain, five Eastern. Thanks both.

**Rachel Ito:** Thank you.

**Mark Kessler:** Thanks, Alex. Make it happen.

# Call transcript — Harbor Health — 2026-11-04

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Erin Walsh (Head of Customer Success, Shiftpoint), Grace Moreno (Practice Operations Manager, Harbor Health)

**Alex Chen:** Good morning, Grace! Thanks for joining. I wanted to be on this one to do a proper handover. This is Erin Walsh — Erin is your Customer Success lead from here on.

**Grace Moreno:** Hi Erin! So nice to meet you. Alex has said lovely things.

**Erin Walsh:** Hi Grace, great to meet you too. And congratulations — I know you ran a long evaluation, so it's exciting to finally get going.

**Grace Moreno:** Thank you so much. Honestly, I'm relieved. Ben signed, the invoice is with AP, and now I just want my clinic leads to stop calling me at nine p.m. about who's covering X-ray.

**Erin Walsh:** [laughs] That's what we're here for. So I'll lead today, and Alex will jump in where it's about what you bought. Just so we're all on the same page: you're on Pro, eight clinics, with payroll export included, and the onboarding package. Right?

**Alex Chen:** That's right. Pro for all eight clinics, payroll export is part of Pro, and onboarding is the full package — setup, data import and two training sessions.

**Grace Moreno:** Yes, eight clinics. That's what Ben signed.

**Erin Walsh:** Perfect. So the main thing I want to agree today is the rollout plan. Alex mentioned you were thinking about two waves?

**Grace Moreno:** Yes. I don't want all eight clinics switching at once in December. My idea is four and four. Wave one would be Bay View, Third Ward, Wauwatosa and West Allis. Those leads are the most comfortable with tech, and Bay View is our biggest.

**Erin Walsh:** Makes sense.

**Grace Moreno:** And then wave two is Brookfield, Greenfield, Glendale and Oak Creek.

**Erin Walsh:** Great. I've got wave one: Bay View, Third Ward, Wauwatosa, West Allis. Wave two: Brookfield, Greenfield, Glendale, Oak Creek. And the reason for that split is mostly the leads?

**Grace Moreno:** Mostly the leads, and Oak Creek and Glendale are short a radiology tech right now, so I'd rather not change their process in the middle of that.

**Erin Walsh:** Smart. Now, the credential piece is the big one for you — making sure every shift has at least one RN and one rad tech. Pro has the compliance rules for that, so the first thing Marco will do is set up those rules per clinic.

**Grace Moreno:** Marco is…?

**Erin Walsh:** Sorry — Marco Rossi, our Onboarding Manager. He runs the onboarding package hands-on. I'll be your main contact overall, Marco does the setup and training. His first session with you is Tuesday, November seventeenth.

**Grace Moreno:** The seventeenth. Okay, let me write that down. That works.

**Erin Walsh:** Before that, the one thing we need from you is the staff list. Names, roles, which clinic, and credentials — RN, MA, rad tech, front desk. About two hundred sixty people?

**Grace Moreno:** About two sixty, yes. Not the providers, they're scheduled separately.

**Erin Walsh:** Right, just the hourly staff. Could you get us that list by November thirteenth? That gives Marco a few days to import before the session.

**Grace Moreno:** By the thirteenth, yes. I'll have to pull it from two places, but that's fine.

**Erin Walsh:** Great. Marco will send you the template so it's one format.

**Grace Moreno:** Thank you, that helps. Now — payroll. Ben's big thing was that payroll export works from day one. He mentioned it to Alex several times, I think.

**Alex Chen:** He did. [laughs] Every call.

**Erin Walsh:** So our suggestion is we test the payroll export in wave one. Those four clinics run one full pay period on Shiftpoint, we export the approved hours, and your payroll team checks it against what they'd normally do. Then by the time wave two goes live, it's proven.

**Grace Moreno:** I love that. Ben will love that. Can I tell him that's the plan?

**Erin Walsh:** Please do. Marco will confirm the exact dates on the seventeenth, once he's seen your data. I don't want to give you a go-live date today before he's looked at it, but the goal is to have you running before the holiday staffing peak.

**Grace Moreno:** That's all I want. December is our crazy month — flu season, holidays, everyone wants time off.

**Erin Walsh:** Understood. We'll plan around that. One more practical thing — the staff app. Have you thought about how you'll tell the clinic teams?

**Grace Moreno:** A little. I was going to do it at our monthly all-hands, but that's not until the eighth of December.

**Erin Walsh:** For wave one I'd suggest earlier. What works well at other clinic groups is a short message from you, plus a one-page "how to download the app" sheet we give you, and then each clinic lead walks their team through it at shift change. Takes ten minutes.

**Grace Moreno:** Oh, that's good. Our MAs will be fine. Some of the older nurses will grumble, but they grumble about everything. [laughs]

**Erin Walsh:** [laughs] Totally normal. Reminders also go out by text, so nobody misses a shift because they didn't install the app on day one.

**Grace Moreno:** Okay, good. And the clinic leads — do they need their own training?

**Erin Walsh:** Yes, that's the second of the two training sessions in the onboarding package. Session one with Marco is the setup with you — clinics, shifts, credential rules. Session two is for the leads, how to build the week, approve swaps, react to a compliance alert.

**Grace Moreno:** Can we record those? My Oak Creek lead works evenings.

**Erin Walsh:** Yes, Marco records them, and you'll get the link afterward.

**Grace Moreno:** Thank you so much. That really helps.

**Erin Walsh:** Of course. Who should be on the session on the seventeenth from your side, besides you?

**Grace Moreno:** Me, and probably the Bay View lead, since she's wave one and our biggest. I'll ask Ben if someone from payroll should join for the export part.

**Erin Walsh:** That would be great — even fifteen minutes of their time. Alex, anything from the sales side I'm missing?

**Alex Chen:** Just the paperwork side: everything Ben signed is on file, and the invoice went to AP — twenty-one thousand one hundred twenty for the year, that's eight clinics at two twenty per clinic per month on Pro, plus the three thousand for onboarding. So nothing open there. From here on, Erin is your first call for anything — I'll still be around, but she owns it.

**Grace Moreno:** Okay. Thank you both. And honestly, if this goes well, maybe adding two more clinics next year — we're looking at Racine and Kenosha.

**Erin Walsh:** Great, let's get these eight live first.

**Grace Moreno:** Of course, of course. Nothing decided, it's just something the founders talk about. I just wanted you to know.

**Alex Chen:** Good to know, thanks Grace. Let's get the eight running smoothly and we'll see from there.

**Erin Walsh:** So, to recap. One, eight clinics on Pro, two waves: Bay View, Third Ward, Wauwatosa, West Allis first, then Brookfield, Greenfield, Glendale, Oak Creek. Two, staff list of about two sixty, by November thirteenth, Marco sends the template. Three, payroll export gets tested in wave one. Four, first onboarding session with Marco Rossi on Tuesday the seventeenth. I'll send this in writing today.

**Grace Moreno:** Perfect. Thank you so much, Erin. And Alex, thank you for everything.

**Alex Chen:** My pleasure, Grace. Talk soon.

**Erin Walsh:** Bye, Grace!

**Alex Chen:** No problem. I'll start with the operations side and we can do the HR questions when he's on. Before I share, can I just play back what I have, so I'm showing you the right things?

**Olivia Bennett:** Please.

**Alex Chen:** Six hotels, about three hundred ten hourly staff. Every department head at every hotel keeps their own spreadsheet. Housekeeping overtime runs about twelve percent on high-occupancy weekends, front desk no-shows around five percent, and all in about thirty-five hours a week across the group goes into rotas.

**Olivia Bennett:** That's right. And honestly, housekeeping is where the money goes. A convention weekend at Streeterville, we're at ninety-eight percent, and the following Tuesday we're at thirty-five. The schedule doesn't move with that. It's on a whiteboard.

**Alex Chen:** Got it. So let me share my screen. This is the rota builder, and I've set it up like your River North hotel. You can see the departments across the top here: housekeeping, front desk, night audit, F&B, maintenance.

**Olivia Bennett:** Each department is its own template?

**Alex Chen:** Exactly. Each department has a template — the standard shifts and how many people you need on each. So housekeeping might have a seven a.m. room-attendant shift and a turndown shift. And then each week you do this: "copy last week". Everything from last week rolls forward, and you adjust.

**Olivia Bennett:** And if occupancy is different next week?

**Alex Chen:** Then the housekeeping manager adds or removes shifts from the template right here, and those open shifts go out to the team in the app. Whoever wants the extra hours picks them up. On Core it doesn't pull occupancy automatically — that would be the forecasting on Pro — but most hotel customers on Core just look at the occupancy report and adjust the template. It takes a few minutes instead of an afternoon.

**Olivia Bennett:** That's fine. I don't need it to be magic, I need it in one place.

**Alex Chen:** That's the next part. This is the hotel view. One screen per hotel, all departments, the whole week. Scheduled hours, overtime warnings in red.

**Olivia Bennett:** Oh, that's nice. That's what I want. Can I see all six at once?

**Alex Chen:** Yes — this drop-down at the top. Group view, and then you click into any hotel.

**Olivia Bennett:** I like the per-hotel view a lot. Right now if I want to know what O'Hare is doing next weekend I have to email three people.

**Alex Chen:** That's what we hear a lot. Front desk is the same idea, but it runs twenty-four seven, so the template has three shifts including night audit.

**Olivia Bennett:** And swaps? Our front desk agents swap constantly. Right now they agree between themselves and tell the manager afterward. Sometimes they don't tell the manager.

**Alex Chen:** [laughs] That's very common. Let me show you the phone. An agent taps her shift, taps "offer swap", and anyone at that hotel who's qualified for front desk gets the request. Somebody accepts, and the front office manager gets one approval card — approve or decline. The rota updates itself, so the manager always knows who's actually coming in.

**Olivia Bennett:** Can a housekeeper pick up a front desk shift?

**Alex Chen:** Only if you mark her as qualified for front desk. Each person has the roles they can work, so a swap or open shift only goes to the right people.

**Olivia Bennett:** Good. And can staff work at two hotels? We share some housekeeping between River North and Streeterville on busy weekends.

**Alex Chen:** Yes. A person can belong to more than one hotel, and they'll see open shifts at both. The hours roll up per person, so if someone's getting close to overtime across the two hotels, the manager sees it.

**Olivia Bennett:** That's actually one of our blind spots. Each hotel only sees its own hours.

**Alex Chen:** That's a common one in groups. And the time clock — staff clock in on the phone, and it checks with GPS that they're actually at the hotel.

**Olivia Bennett:** Some of housekeeping may not love using their own phone for that.

**Alex Chen:** That comes up in most hotel groups. Usually it settles within a few weeks, once people see swaps get approved in minutes. Marcus may have a view on that from the HR side.

**Olivia Bennett:** Okay. Ah — Marcus just joined.

**Marcus Reed:** Hi, sorry I'm late. Hi Alex.

**Alex Chen:** Hi Marcus, no worries at all. We just went through the rota templates and the per-hotel view. I know you had questions from the HR side.

**Marcus Reed:** A few, yes. First one: our housekeeping and stewarding staff are union at four of the hotels. Extra shifts have to be offered by seniority. How do you handle that?

**Alex Chen:** Good question. So when a manager posts an open shift, they can set approval rules. Everyone can request it, but the manager sees the requests sorted by a seniority field we import from your HR data, and approves in that order. So the rule lives in the approval step.

**Marcus Reed:** So it's not automatic, but the manager sees the order.

**Alex Chen:** Right. The manager sees the order and approves from the top. Several of our hotel customers do it that way.

**Marcus Reed:** Okay. That could work. Second: languages. A lot of our housekeeping team prefers Spanish, and at Evanston and Oak Brook we have a big Polish-speaking group.

**Alex Chen:** The staff app supports Spanish today — each person picks their language. Polish is on the roadmap, but I honestly can't commit to a date, so I don't want you to plan around it.

**Marcus Reed:** Fair. Thank you for being honest. Spanish covers most of them.

**Olivia Bennett:** Alex, can you go over pricing once more, so Marcus has it too?

**Alex Chen:** Of course. For six hotels I'd recommend Core — rota builder, swaps and open shifts, time clock, messaging. Core is a hundred fifty dollars per location per month, billed yearly. Six hotels comes to ten thousand eight hundred a year. Onboarding is optional under ten locations, and you mentioned you'd rather set it up yourselves, so I'd leave it out.

**Olivia Bennett:** Good, that matches your corrected email.

**Alex Chen:** It does. And again, sorry about the mix-up in September.

**Olivia Bennett:** It's fine. You caught it.

**Marcus Reed:** Is there a break-rule feature? Illinois has some meal-break requirements.

**Alex Chen:** Break rules and the compliance alerts are part of Pro. On Core, you'd still see hours and overtime. If that becomes important, you can move to Pro later. For what Olivia described, Core is the right fit.

**Marcus Reed:** Okay. I'll note it.

**Olivia Bennett:** So, from my side, I'm positive. I'd like a written offer, and then I'll review with Marcus.

**Alex Chen:** Great. I can have the offer to you by Monday, November second. Core, six hotels, ten thousand eight hundred a year.

**Olivia Bennett:** Monday is fine. I'll be honest about timing — we have budget sign-offs in early December, so I'll decide by December fourth.

**Alex Chen:** That works. I'll make the offer valid until December fourth, then. And I won't chase you — maybe a short check-in around the twentieth to see if Marcus has more questions?

**Olivia Bennett:** That would be fine.

**Marcus Reed:** I'll send my questions by email if I have any.

**Alex Chen:** Perfect. So: offer Monday the second, check-in around the twentieth, your decision by December fourth. Thanks both, have a good weekend.

**Olivia Bennett:** Thank you, Alex. Thank you for the clear overview.

**Marcus Reed:** Thanks.

# Call transcript — Pine & Pebble Home — 2026-11-02

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Hannah Clarke (VP Stores, Pine & Pebble Home)

**Alex Chen:** Hi Hannah, Alex here. Thanks for taking the call.

**Hannah Clarke:** Hi Alex! Of course. Jake wouldn't stop talking about you guys, so here I am. [laughs]

**Alex Chen:** That's nice to hear. Jake's been a great customer — seven taprooms up in Fort Collins. So, I've got about thirty minutes blocked, but I'd love to hear the story first. Where are you today?

**Hannah Clarke:** Okay. So, twenty-five stores across Colorado, Utah and New Mexico, about seven hundred hourly, a hundred fifty more in holiday season. Sixteen stores in Colorado, six in Utah, three in New Mexico.

**Alex Chen:** And those seasonal folks start when?

**Hannah Clarke:** They're starting now, basically. Mid-November through early January. And onboarding a hundred fifty people into a schedule that doesn't work is, um — it's a lot.

**Alex Chen:** What are you using for scheduling today?

**Hannah Clarke:** The scheduling module in our POS. It's rigid. There are no swaps on mobile. If an associate wants to swap a Saturday, they text the manager, the manager changes it in the back office, and half the time the punches don't match what's scheduled.

**Alex Chen:** And what does that cost you in time?

**Hannah Clarke:** My managers spend a full day a week on schedules. Okay, maybe five hours, but it feels like a full day. Across twenty-five stores, that's, what, a hundred twenty-five hours a week.

**Alex Chen:** That's a lot of hours that aren't on the floor.

**Hannah Clarke:** Exactly. In Q4 they should be on the floor selling. And overtime in Q4 is around ten percent of hours. And then payroll — Jorge, our payroll manager, his team spends two days every pay period fixing missed punches and premiums by hand.

**Alex Chen:** Two days every period. Okay. Is that mostly because the punches don't line up with the schedule?

**Hannah Clarke:** Partly. And partly because Colorado, Utah and New Mexico have different rules, and the POS doesn't know any of that.

**Alex Chen:** That's helpful. I spent three years in payroll software before Shiftpoint, so this is close to my heart. [laughs] Let me ask about the future side too. Do you ever staff from traffic? Like, Saturday at Cherry Creek versus a Tuesday in Pueblo?

**Hannah Clarke:** We want to. Right now it's gut feel. The managers look at last year and guess. And honestly, with the predictive scheduling discussions in Colorado, my board is asking how we'd even comply with posting schedules in advance.

**Alex Chen:** Got it. So based on that, I'd recommend our Pro plan, not Core. Core gives you the rota builder, swaps in the app, time clock and messaging. Pro adds three things that map to what you just said: labor forecasting from your sales and traffic data, compliance alerts — breaks, overtime, fair-workweek type rules — and payroll export is included.

**Hannah Clarke:** So the forecasting would use the POS traffic?

**Alex Chen:** Sales and footfall data, yes. It suggests how many people you need per hour, and the manager adjusts. And the payroll export means approved hours go straight to payroll, so Jorge's team isn't retyping things.

**Hannah Clarke:** Jorge's going to have a hundred questions about that.

**Alex Chen:** Good. I'd much rather he asks them before than after. The multi-state rules especially — I'd like to show him that live.

**Hannah Clarke:** Okay. So what does Pro cost?

**Alex Chen:** Pro is two hundred twenty dollars per location per month, billed yearly. For twenty-five stores that's sixty-six thousand a year. And then there's a one-time onboarding package, three thousand dollars, which is required at ten locations and up — that covers setup, importing your people and two training sessions.

**Hannah Clarke:** Sixty-six. Hm. That's higher than I hoped, but if forecasting works it pays for itself.

**Alex Chen:** That's the way most of our customers look at it. If the managers get even half of those hundred twenty-five hours back, and Q4 overtime comes down a couple of points, the math gets there quickly. I'd like to build that with your real numbers.

**Hannah Clarke:** Yeah, that's going to matter, because anything over fifty thousand goes to Megan. Megan Liu, our CFO. She signs off on everything over fifty K.

**Alex Chen:** Good to know. What will Megan want to see?

**Hannah Clarke:** An ROI story. She told me last time, "I want an ROI model, not slides." [laughs] She's very direct.

**Alex Chen:** I like that. We'll make it about your numbers: manager hours, Q4 overtime, payroll fixing time. Have you looked at anyone else?

**Hannah Clarke:** I glanced at Crewlane. Honestly, I didn't love the app, and Jake said yours is better. We're not really evaluating them.

**Alex Chen:** Okay. And the POS vendor — any contract that stops you from moving scheduling out?

**Hannah Clarke:** No, scheduling is just a module. We'd keep the POS and turn the module off.

**Alex Chen:** Perfect. Can I ask a couple more things about the stores themselves, so the demo is relevant?

**Hannah Clarke:** Go for it.

**Alex Chen:** How are the stores staffed — is it one manager per store doing the schedule, or department leads?

**Hannah Clarke:** One store manager, and in the bigger stores, Cherry Creek, Sugar House, Nob Hill, there's an assistant manager who does the stockroom and delivery crew. So two people touching the schedule in maybe eight stores.

**Alex Chen:** And do people work across stores?

**Hannah Clarke:** All the time in Denver. Highlands, Lowry and Cherry Creek share associates. In Salt Lake, Sugar House and Downtown share. And the delivery crew covers whole regions.

**Alex Chen:** Okay, that's useful. In Shiftpoint a person can belong to several stores and see open shifts at each, and hours roll up per person — so you'd catch overtime that happens because someone worked at two stores in one week.

**Hannah Clarke:** Oh, that happens constantly in December. Nobody sees it until payroll.

**Alex Chen:** That's exactly the kind of thing Jorge will want to see. And the seasonal hires — how do they get onboarded today?

**Hannah Clarke:** Paper, then the manager types them into the POS. It takes forever, and they don't get their schedule until they show up for training.

**Alex Chen:** With the app they'd get an invite by text, download it, and see their first shifts the same day. We can show that in the demo too.

**Hannah Clarke:** Yes, please. My managers would love that.

**Alex Chen:** Great. So what I'd suggest as the next step is a proper demo — rota builder, swaps, forecasting, and especially the payroll export — with Jorge in the room. Can we get Jorge on?

**Hannah Clarke:** Yes, let's get Jorge in the room. When?

**Alex Chen:** How about Tuesday, November tenth, at nine-thirty?

**Hannah Clarke:** Let me look... Tuesday the tenth, nine-thirty works for me. Jorge is usually free mornings. I'll confirm with him.

**Alex Chen:** Great. I'll send the invite to both of you for Tuesday the tenth, nine-thirty, about forty-five minutes. And before that I'll send you a short recap with the pricing written out, so you have it.

**Hannah Clarke:** Perfect. Let's keep momentum. Oh — do you have a retail example? Something I could share with Megan?

**Alex Chen:** Let me check what we can share and get back to you. I'll be honest, our case studies are more restaurants and clinics, but let me see what's best.

**Hannah Clarke:** That's fine. Okay, thanks Alex!

**Alex Chen:** Thanks, Hannah. Talk soon.

# Call transcript — SparklePro Cleaning — 2026-11-03

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Kevin O'Brien (COO, SparklePro Cleaning), Lisa Tran (Branch Operations Lead, SparklePro Cleaning)

**Alex Chen:** Morning, Kevin. Morning, Lisa. Thanks for moving things around for this.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Morning, Alex. Sorry about last week, I had a client walk-through I couldn't move.

**Lisa Tran:** Good morning!

**Alex Chen:** Totally fine. So, quick recap from our discovery call, and then I'll show you the product. Kevin, correct me if anything's changed.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Sure. Fourteen branches, about six hundred fifty cleaners, almost all nights. We clean offices, schools, medical buildings — around four hundred buildings a night.

**Alex Chen:** And the big numbers were about six percent of shifts going uncovered at short notice, around ninety thousand in client credits last year for missed cleans, and branch leads spending about six hours a week each on rotas and calling around.

**Kevin O'Brien:** That's it. And supervisors driving to buildings at ten p.m. to see if anybody showed up. That's the one that drives me nuts.

**Alex Chen:** Okay, so that's where I'll start. Let me share my screen. This is the manager view, and I've set it up as if it were your Omaha Central branch. Each building is a site under the branch, and the shifts are the nightly cleans.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Okay.

**Alex Chen:** Here's the open-shift flow. Say a cleaner at the Lincoln North branch calls in sick at four in the afternoon. The branch lead clicks on that shift, hits "post as open shift", and everybody qualified at that branch gets a notification on their phone. First person to grab it, the lead approves, done.

**Kevin O'Brien:** And the lead doesn't have to call anybody.

**Alex Chen:** Doesn't have to call anybody. And they can see right here which shifts are still uncovered for tonight, in red.

**Lisa Tran:** Can the cleaner see which building it is before they take it?

**Alex Chen:** Yes — the building, the address, the hours. Let me switch to the phone view so you see what they see. Here: "Open shift, tonight, 6 to 10 p.m., Midtown Medical Building." Tap "pick up".

**Lisa Tran:** Okay, that's clear. Is that in Spanish too? About half our crews prefer Spanish.

**Alex Chen:** Yes. Each person picks their language in the app, and Spanish is fully supported.

**Lisa Tran:** Great. And the phones — a lot of our people are on prepaid Androids, some of them pretty old.

**Alex Chen:** Older Android phones are supported. And if someone doesn't install the app at all, they still get shift reminders by text. They just can't pick up open shifts themselves.

**Lisa Tran:** That's fine. Most of them will use it if it gets them extra hours.

**Alex Chen:** That's usually what happens. Now, Kevin, the thing you said was the must-have: GPS clock-in. When the cleaner arrives at the building, they clock in on the phone, and the app checks they're actually at that address. If they try to clock in from home, the lead gets flagged.

**Kevin O'Brien:** So my supervisors can stop driving around at night.

**Alex Chen:** That's the idea. This board — live attendance for tonight, every building. Green, clocked in on site. Gray, not started yet. Red, should've started and nobody's there.

**Kevin O'Brien:** That red one is a client credit waiting to happen.

**Alex Chen:** Exactly — and you'd see it at six-fifteen, not the next morning when the client calls.

**Lisa Tran:** What about cleaners who cover two branches? Council Bluffs and Omaha Central share a lot of people.

**Alex Chen:** A person can belong to more than one branch. They'd see open shifts at both, and their hours roll up, so the leads can see if someone's heading into overtime across the two.

**Lisa Tran:** Oh, that's good. Right now we only find that out on payroll day.

**Kevin O'Brien:** How do the branch leads talk to the crews? Right now it's a group text per branch and it's chaos.

**Alex Chen:** There's messaging per location. A lead can send an announcement to the whole branch — "the school on Dodge is closed Friday, crews reassigned" — and everybody gets it in the app, or by text if they don't have it.

**Kevin O'Brien:** And people can't reply-all with thumbs up?

**Alex Chen:** [laughs] No reply-all. It's announcements.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Sold. [laughs] Just kidding. Partly.

**Lisa Tran:** One more — turnover is really high for us, like seventy percent a year. How fast can we add a new hire?

**Alex Chen:** The lead adds them with a name and phone number, they get a text invite, download the app, and they can see their shifts the same day. Removing someone who leaves is one click, and their future shifts go back to open.

**Lisa Tran:** That would save me a lot of time. We add five or ten people a week across the branches.

**Alex Chen:** That's exactly why we built it that way. A lot of our cleaning and security customers have the same churn.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Okay. I like this a lot. Lisa?

**Lisa Tran:** I like it too. How long does training take for the branch leads?

**Alex Chen:** For fourteen branches you'd have the onboarding package — that's setup, importing your people and buildings, and two training sessions. Most leads are comfortable after the first session.

**Lisa Tran:** Okay, good.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Alright. What's the damage?

**Alex Chen:** [laughs] Fair. For you it's Core — open shifts, swaps, GPS time clock, messaging. Core is a hundred fifty dollars per location per month, billed yearly. Fourteen branches, that's twenty-five thousand two hundred a year. And the onboarding package is three thousand one-time, which is required at ten locations and up.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Per branch, not per building.

**Alex Chen:** Per branch. So per location the way you organize it — the buildings live under the branch.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Okay. Is Crewlane cheaper? Somebody mentioned them at a conference.

**Alex Chen:** Usually a bit, but their app is weaker. And for you the app is the whole thing — if crews don't pick up open shifts on their phones, you're back to the phone tree.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Fair enough.

**Alex Chen:** And just to tie it back: if you're at ninety thousand a year in client credits, and this cuts the uncovered shifts even by a third, that's more than the subscription.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Yeah, I did that math in my head already. Look — send me the offer and let's walk through it next week. If it looks like this, I'm good.

**Alex Chen:** Great. I'll put together a written offer: Core for fourteen branches, twenty-five thousand two hundred a year, plus three thousand onboarding. When's good next week for a walkthrough?

**Kevin O'Brien:** Wednesday morning?

**Alex Chen:** Wednesday, November eleventh, ten a.m. my time — that's eleven your time. Does that work?

**Kevin O'Brien:** Eleven Central on Wednesday works.

**Lisa Tran:** I'll put it in Kevin's calendar. I may not join, but I'll be around for questions.

**Alex Chen:** Perfect. So: I'll send the offer ahead of time so you can read it first, and we'll walk through it Wednesday the eleventh. Anybody else on your side who should see it?

**Kevin O'Brien:** I'll forward it to Ray, our controller. He'll want to see payment terms. But it's my call.

**Alex Chen:** Sounds good. Thanks Kevin, thanks Lisa.

**Kevin O'Brien:** Thanks, Alex.

**Lisa Tran:** Thank you, bye!

# Call transcript — Ironclad Guard Services — 2026-11-03

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Fatima Khan (Procurement Lead, Ironclad Guard Services), Daniel Price (Operations Manager, Ironclad Guard Services)

**Alex Chen:** Hi Fatima, hi Daniel. Thanks for setting this up.

**Fatima Khan:** Hi Alex, thanks for making the time. Daniel's joining from dispatch.

**Daniel Price:** Afternoon. Copy, I'm here.

**Alex Chen:** Great. So, Fatima, you asked for a terms call. Want to take it from the top?

**Fatima Khan:** Sure. We've reviewed your proposal for thirty sites at list, fifty-four thousand plus onboarding. Overall it's in line with what we expected, and Daniel's team is keen.

**Daniel Price:** Very keen.

**Fatima Khan:** We have one ask. Given we're committing all thirty sites up front, we'd like 10% off the subscription. If you can do that, we can sign this month.

**Alex Chen:** Okay. That's a reasonable ask for a thirty-site commitment. Ten percent I can do.

**Fatima Khan:** Oh — good. That's easier than I expected. [laughs]

**Alex Chen:** [laughs] I'd rather spend our time on the rollout. So let me restate the numbers so we're all looking at the same thing. Core, thirty sites, at a hundred fifty per location per month billed yearly is fifty-four thousand a year at list. Ten percent off the subscription brings it to forty-eight thousand six hundred a year. Onboarding stays at three thousand, as quoted. So year one is fifty-one thousand six hundred.

**Fatima Khan:** Forty-eight six plus three, fifty-one six for year one. That matches my math.

**Alex Chen:** Good. And just to be clear, the ten percent is on the subscription, not on onboarding.

**Fatima Khan:** Understood, that's fine. On payment terms — your proposal says yearly up front.

**Alex Chen:** That's right, yearly up front is our standard.

**Fatima Khan:** That's acceptable. We pay our other software vendors that way too. I just wanted to confirm.

**Alex Chen:** Great. Daniel, from the operations side — anything that's changed since the demo?

**Daniel Price:** Bottom line: nothing's changed, it's gotten worse. Last weekend we had four call-outs between midnight and four. My dispatcher was on the phone for two hours filling one hospital post.

**Alex Chen:** That's the three a.m. phone call you told me about.

**Daniel Price:** That's the one. Overtime's still running about nineteen percent of hours, and a lot of it we can't bill back.

**Alex Chen:** So with the open-shift flow, that call-out goes to every licensed officer who's qualified for that post, in the app, and whoever picks it up shows up in the schedule. And the GPS clock-in at the start and end of the shift gives you proof they were on post.

**Daniel Price:** Copy that. That's what sold my dispatchers. One question they asked me after the demo. Officers aren't supposed to be on their phones on post. Some clients are strict about that, the data centers especially.

**Alex Chen:** Right, we talked about that in discovery. The GPS clock-in is only at the start and the end of the shift. During the shift the app doesn't need anything from them. And open shifts are something they'd look at off duty.

**Daniel Price:** Good. And if an officer clocks in from the parking lot of the wrong site?

**Alex Chen:** Then dispatch gets a flag, because the GPS check is against the address of that post. You can set the radius per site — a hospital campus is bigger than an HOA gate.

**Daniel Price:** Copy. The hospital campuses are big. Desert Ridge has three entrances.

**Alex Chen:** Then you'd set a wider radius there. That's part of what Marco sets up with you in onboarding.

**Fatima Khan:** Is that included in the onboarding fee, or extra?

**Alex Chen:** Included. Onboarding covers setup of all thirty sites, importing your officers, and two training sessions. No extras.

**Fatima Khan:** Good. I just want to avoid surprises on the invoice.

**Daniel Price:** And the two dispatchers — I want them trained first. They're the ones who'll live in it.

**Alex Chen:** That makes sense. They'd be in the first training session, and the site supervisors in the second.

**Daniel Price:** Copy. Now — rollout. We'd like to go live in January.

**Alex Chen:** January's a good target. I'll confirm the exact plan with Marco, our onboarding manager, once the order form is in, but a January start for thirty sites is the kind of timeline we normally work with.

**Daniel Price:** And I'd like to pilot at the five hospital sites first. Desert Ridge Medical Center and the other four. They're the posts with the strictest client requirements, so if it works there, it works everywhere.

**Alex Chen:** That's a sensible way to do it. You'd still license all thirty sites from the start, as in the proposal — the pilot is just about the order you roll out in. Marco does phased rollouts a lot.

**Daniel Price:** Understood. All thirty licensed, five go first. Fine with me.

**Fatima Khan:** Yes, that's what we discussed internally as well. We're committing to thirty.

**Alex Chen:** Perfect. And officer guard-card tracking stays in your HR system, like we said in discovery, so Core is still the right plan — you don't need Pro for that.

**Daniel Price:** Correct. HR owns the cards.

**Fatima Khan:** So what happens next on your side?

**Alex Chen:** I'll send you an updated offer — version two — with the ten percent, so forty-eight thousand six hundred a year plus three thousand onboarding, yearly billing. And with it, the order form, so you can review it with legal ahead of time. Then I'd suggest we do an order form review together. Does Monday the sixteenth work? Eleven a.m.?

**Fatima Khan:** Let me check... Monday, November sixteenth at eleven works for me. Daniel?

**Daniel Price:** Eleven on the sixteenth. Works.

**Alex Chen:** Great. Same time zone for once — you're Phoenix, I'm Denver, and this time of year we're both on the same clock.

**Daniel Price:** [laughs] Only half the year.

**Fatima Khan:** I'll also send you a short email today or tomorrow confirming what we discussed, for my records.

**Alex Chen:** That'd be great. I'll reply to that with the updated offer. Anything else either of you needs from me before the sixteenth?

**Fatima Khan:** A W-9 for vendor setup, if you can.

**Alex Chen:** I'll ask our finance team to send it over.

**Daniel Price:** One thing. When we go to the Tucson sites, the supervisor there runs his own little schedule on paper. I want him on the same system as Phoenix from day one, not a separate thing.

**Alex Chen:** That's how it'd be set up — one account, all thirty sites, grouped however you like. Phoenix hospitals, data centers, logistics parks, HOAs, retail, Tucson. Dispatch sees everything; the Tucson supervisor sees his three sites.

**Daniel Price:** Copy that. Bottom line, that's what I need. Otherwise nothing from me. Looking forward to getting this going.

**Alex Chen:** Same here. So, recap: ten percent off the subscription, forty-eight six a year, onboarding three thousand as quoted, yearly billing. Offer version two and the order form from me before the sixteenth. Order form review Monday, November sixteenth, eleven a.m. Pilot at the five hospital sites, target go-live January, which I'll confirm with onboarding.

**Fatima Khan:** That's correct. Thank you, Alex.

**Daniel Price:** Copy. Thanks.

**Alex Chen:** Thanks both. Talk soon.

# Call transcript — Little Acorns Childcare — 2026-10-28

Participants: Alex Chen (Account Executive, Shiftpoint), Emily Carter (Executive Director, Little Acorns Childcare), Sam Wood (Center Operations Coordinator, Little Acorns Childcare)

**Alex Chen:** Hi Emily, hi Sam. Thanks for joining. Emily, good to see you again.

**Emily Carter:** Hi Alex. Thank you for doing this. I brought Sam, because Sam is the one who actually lives in the schedules.

**Sam Wood:** Hey. Yeah, I'm the floater guy. [laughs]

**Alex Chen:** Perfect, then you're exactly who I want to hear from. Emily, just to make sure I've got the picture right before I share my screen?

**Emily Carter:** Sure. Eleven centers, about two hundred ninety staff. Lead teachers, assistant teachers, floaters, and our cooks. Every classroom has to meet ratio every hour, so every sick call is a scramble.

**Alex Chen:** And today it's the paper grids per classroom, photographed and posted, and floaters by text.

**Sam Wood:** Before seven a.m., usually. My phone starts going at six-fifteen.

**Alex Chen:** And the directors spend about six hours a week each on the grids, overtime around eight percent, mostly floaters, and twice this year a classroom had to close for a morning.

**Emily Carter:** Twice. And that's the part that really hurts — for families, and for the teachers who feel responsible. Our teachers are the heart of this.

**Alex Chen:** Understood. Let me share. So this is the rota builder, and I set it up like your North Boulder center. Instead of departments I made each classroom a row group — Infants, Toddlers, Preschool, Pre-K — and then the kitchen.

**Emily Carter:** Oh, that's nice. That looks like our grid.

**Alex Chen:** That's on purpose. Each classroom has a template — the standard shifts and the minimum number of staff you need on each shift. So for the infant room you'd say, minimum two people from seven to nine, three from nine to three, and so on.

**Sam Wood:** And you set that once?

**Alex Chen:** Set it once, then every week you hit "copy last week" and adjust. If a shift in the template doesn't have enough people assigned, it shows up as unfilled, here, in orange.

**Sam Wood:** Okay.

**Alex Chen:** Now the floater piece. When someone calls in sick, the director marks that shift as open, and it goes out to the floaters and anyone qualified at nearby centers in the app. Sam, you'd see all open shifts across all eleven centers in one place.

**Sam Wood:** Instead of my texts. Okay, that I like.

**Alex Chen:** Then on Pro — which is what I'd recommend for you — there are the compliance alerts. Breaks, overtime. So if a teacher is about to go into overtime because she picked up a second shift, the director sees it before approving.

**Emily Carter:** That's important. A lot of overtime is just tired teachers saying yes.

**Alex Chen:** Right. And the third piece is payroll export. Approved hours go straight to payroll, so nobody retypes the grids at the end of the period.

**Emily Carter:** Monica will appreciate that. She's our finance and admin manager.

**Sam Wood:** Can I ask something? Can it tell me when a room is under ratio?

**Alex Chen:** Good question, and I want to be precise, because I don't want to oversell this. What Shiftpoint does is: you set the minimum staffing per shift in the template, and if a shift is unfilled — because someone called in sick and nobody picked it up — it flags it. It does not calculate ratio from how many children are actually in the room. There's no dedicated ratio calculation from attendance.

**Sam Wood:** So if I set the minimums right, it tells me which room is short a person.

**Alex Chen:** Exactly. It tells you which shift is short against the minimum you set. It doesn't know if four kids went home early.

**Sam Wood:** Okay, that'd still help. Honestly most of my mornings are just "who's missing where".

**Emily Carter:** That's fine for us. The directors know the enrollment; they just need to see the gaps.

**Alex Chen:** Great. Labor forecasting on Pro can use enrollment numbers as an input, so directors get a suggestion for how many people a week needs. But the ratio itself stays with the directors.

**Sam Wood:** Another one — floaters move between centers. Like, I might send someone from Louisville to Superior at seven, then back at noon. Can it handle that?

**Alex Chen:** Yes. A floater can belong to several centers, and you can give them a shift at Superior in the morning and Louisville in the afternoon. Their hours roll up across both, so if they're heading into overtime the director sees it before approving.

**Sam Wood:** Oh, that's huge. That's where all our overtime comes from.

**Emily Carter:** And the teachers — will they find it easy? Some of them aren't very techy.

**Alex Chen:** The app is basically two screens: "my shifts" and "open shifts". And anyone who doesn't install it still gets reminders by text. What usually happens is the younger teachers start using it in week one and show everyone else.

**Emily Carter:** That sounds like our centers. [laughs]

**Alex Chen:** And the cooks — they'd just be another role, with their own template in the kitchen row. They wouldn't see classroom shifts unless you mark them as qualified.

**Emily Carter:** Good. We have some cooks who also have their teaching certificate and help out at lunch.

**Alex Chen:** Then you'd give them both roles, and they'd see both kinds of open shifts.

**Sam Wood:** And can directors message their whole center? Like, "staff meeting moved to Thursday"?

**Alex Chen:** Yes, there's messaging per location. Announcements go to the app, or by text for anyone without it.

**Sam Wood:** Nice. That replaces at least one of my group texts.

**Emily Carter:** Okay. Can you tell me what this would cost? I'll need to explain it to the board.

**Alex Chen:** Of course. Pro is two hundred twenty dollars per location per month, billed yearly. Eleven centers, that's twenty-nine thousand and forty dollars a year. Plus the onboarding package, three thousand one-time, which is required at ten locations and up. That covers setup, importing your staff and two training sessions.

**Emily Carter:** Twenty-nine thousand and forty, plus three thousand.

**Alex Chen:** That's right. So thirty-two thousand and forty in year one, then twenty-nine forty a year after that.

**Emily Carter:** Our board approves anything over twenty-five thousand, so this goes to them. They meet on the seventeenth of November.

**Alex Chen:** Okay. What would help you most for the board?

**Emily Carter:** A clear written offer. And the story — the classroom closures, the directors' time. I want to make sure we get this right.

**Alex Chen:** I can do that. I'll send a written offer by Friday, October thirtieth, Pro for eleven centers at twenty-nine thousand and forty a year, plus three thousand onboarding, so you have it well before the board. Should I copy Monica?

**Emily Carter:** Yes, please copy Monica. She prepares the board packet.

**Sam Wood:** And training — would that be me?

**Alex Chen:** You and the directors, most likely. Our onboarding manager, Marco, runs the two training sessions. We can figure out the details once the board decides.

**Emily Carter:** Good. Okay — send it over, I'll take it to the board on the 17th.

**Alex Chen:** Will do. Offer to you and Monica by Friday the thirtieth. And if questions come up before the board, just email me and we'll find a time to talk.

**Emily Carter:** Thank you, Alex. This was really helpful.

**Sam Wood:** Yeah, thanks. Cool stuff.

**Alex Chen:** Thanks both. Have a good rest of the week.
